items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I joined the band. When I joined the band, McCoy Tyner was there.

ctx.x: This is well before you made that Killer Joe record with him.

Yeah. I joined the band. When I joined the band, McCoy Tyner was there. Joe Henderson, Bill Hardman, Junie Booth, and Art. They played music that would move you right off the stage if you didn’t hold on. It was so strong that it was frightening. You can imagine, with McCoy and Art in the same band. And the bass player, Junie Booth, was as strong as they were, a real young guy, but just played fantastic.

items.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: on “Angle Eyes” Slide Hampton conducted that one

ctx.x: Say again? Conductor was Bob Belden and then on “Angle Eyes” Slide Hampton conducted that one.
Slide had a lot of good arrangements.
